DEDICATION Prologue The first age of man ended much as it had begun with silence.  At the close of the 22 nd  century, Earth stood empty, bereft of humans, void of their monuments. The beasts once again ruled the planet. The instrument of man's demise, the alien weapon,  unearthed and activated by  humanity , Ignorant of its intent ,  now stood stalwart upon the blue world .  Though Earth stood empty of man, the universe did not. Seeing the end coming, humanity, in a last desperate act to save itself, created the ARC.  With the advanced knowledge gleaned from the alien weapon,  t he last remnants of humanity, twenty thousand souls in all, slept away the ages, aboard the massive ship  as it floated among the darkness of space . Drifting silently through the  void , the vessel waited and watched, until the day it would bring home  Earths  children .  Locked away and frozen, mankind slumbered away the centuries, until at once,  the small pods launched towards the blue planet, hurdling down into the atmosphere like a sudden thunderstorm humanity   returned  home to rebuild the world they had abandoned .  However,  either  by accident or  a  purpose not understood by man or machine,  some did not make the  journey, there pods simply floating in space, eventually falling back to the planet ,  to confront a new world, with new people and new dangers .  This is the story of one such sleeper. ONE CORLISS A time for love, a time for hate, a time for peace and a time for war. - Book of Aurtus The blonde  woman  sat silently at a table in the far corner of the small village  tavern .  Blue  Pipe smoke  highlighted by the muted candle chalices  hung heavy in the air like a thick fog ,  permeating the ancient timbers that  held up the low ceiling, the smoke the lesser of the offensive odors the woman thought ,  crinkling her nose  as yet another tendril of the acrid smoke floated over the worn wooden table  she inhabited ,  her  thin build  would appear delicate to a casual onlooker,  but  to those who stopped and studied the mysterious woman a moment ,  would see the hard muscle framed by the light cotton shirt that hid under the dirty and worn brown leather jacket , the build of someone who knew hard labor and harder living , of one who could take care of herself .  The  dozen or so  patrons covertly shot suspicious glances and whispers in her direction, sky blue eyes and a firmly set alabaster jaw stood partially hidden under a large  brown  leather bolero hat, the scuffs and stains  matching that of the coat and leather pants all of which  told of hard use.  She  sat poised, back straight and body tense, the only motion was the lifting of a dented and scraped tin cup as it disappeared for a moment under the  bolero  only to quickly  reappear , coming back to rest on the table with a light clink , the sound as regular as the tick of a clock .  Subtly shifting her head, the woman caught the whispers  and felt the curious stares as the intensity of the patron’s gazes sent the hairs on the back of her neck to attention.  Corliss  listened to  the uncomfortable shifting of bodies as the old wooden chairs groaned in protest, still using the leather brim as cover,  she reached out with razor sharp senses allowing them to rove  over the room ,  assessing the collection of pistols, swords and other assorted items that peaked from under jackets  and clinked against the wooden seats , not all soldiers   she thought trying to ascertain which was which.  The inn was walking distance to the local barracks and would be frequented by the soldiers of the crown and of the Lord Seer.  The long bastard swords with their black hilts  and teardrop pommels  marked these men and she dismissed them readily, they would pose no threat, she had her royal seal allowing her to work as a warden and they would respect it, however the other patrons would not be so readily swayed she mused still looking over those with weapons that would be considered unorthodox as she spotted filed down scythes and deer antlers , the weapons of farmers .  This was a local tavern, not a place where strangers were seen  often,  when one arrived, they quickly became the object of speculation and suspicion.  Corliss understood this, she had been in more than her fair share of local taverns brought here by duty just as was the case this night , reaching out with  the  finely tuned senses  honed by years of training  her ears  joining  the work of her eyes, listening intently for anyone trying to approach, slowly she lowered one hand under the table running a finger  lightly  along the worn leather of the large belt she wore around her thin waist , fingers were soon rewarded as they found the set of leather tassels, smiling and with practiced ease she loosened the ties   that held the two pistols in place, allowing them to be drawn quickly should the need arise.  This is looking more and more like a gun fight  she thought bitterly as her mind counted the number of firearms in the tavern. Her breath hitched as the sound of the Tavern’s door opened ,  her eyes now drawn to the large wooden  entrance  as the new patron stepped in from the cold.  Corliss tensed as her eyes followed the young man hesitantly entering the establishment. He was a large lad with shoulder length dark hair and an earnest face, his dark eyes wide as he shot nervous glances around the room the patrons turning to regard him with suspicion and a trace of hostility.  The burgundy dragon tattoo on his cheek marked him as a mage and looking around the tavern Corliss could see the glances of mistrust and resentment that greeted the young man.  She had always felt bad for the mages, their abilities separating them from the people, they spent their lives in service, never trusted and never welcome she thought, but there had been a time when all of these people’s great grandfathers would have had that same power, so was it mistrust or was it jealousy she mused, watching intently as  the man quickly crossed the bar and took a place at a corner table away from the crowd of patrons. Part of the world but always separate she thought a small trace of sadness flitting through her mind. She regarded the  mage,  her thoughts drifting ,  Corliss almost missed the door opening a second time, the long creak  broke her from her thoughts  as the hinges  protested  their use.  her  eyes  disappearing once again  under the brim as a distinct and familiar set of footfalls made their way across the dirty wooden planks a thump followed by a scrape and then repeated.  Corliss knew the sound ,  in fact she had been the one to cause the limp that gave the man that distinct gate, a wicked smile spreading across her face as she recalled the incident.  Lowering the bolero  further  Corliss hid her face as the man passed ,   looking  down at the floor  watching  the old worn boots pass the table.  She  carefully reached down  unwrapping  the piece of leather tied to the two hatchets along the back of her belt making the weapons readily available.  Waiting as the man’s odd gate continued towards the bar  she  shifted  subtly   slipping unseen  from the table,  slightly hunching her shoulders and  slouching, she began to weave slightly the effect giving her the look of having had too much to drink and  allowing her to blend in with the  gaggle of peasants gathered around the long wooden bar , it was her ability to hide in plain sight that had garnered her the nickname Ghost within the ranks of the wardens, the crippled  man’s eyes  passing  over  her  without giving her a second look.  Corliss removed the hat revealing high cheekbones and sky-blue eyes framed over a generous mane of long  blonde hair tied back in a tight ponytail , the reveal garnering her more than one appreciative stare from the gathered customers .  Corliss glare d at the gathered men,  around her ,  each set of eyes  dropped quickly  to the floor , refusing the silent challenge  her face held .  Stretching  her back and  cracking  her neck  she let out a sigh of pleasure ,  stepping up behind the new addition to the bar she raised her voice so that everyone could hear .  “ Castigan   Morinth , you are a fugitive of the crown and are bound by law to accompany me to the city of Lester for trial, do you concede?”  The tavern grew quiet  as  patrons began shuffling from the bar, putting distance between themselves and the Warden as eyes  drifted to the crippled man standing by the old bar.  The  man,  just a little taller than Corliss stood there, his brown floor-length coat  rustling  across the worn wood en  floor as he turned to reveal a dark brooding face, a prominent scar from the two’s last encounter ran along the man’s cheek the white of the scar a contrast to his Mediterranean  coloring,  short  black hair and deep brown eyes.  A smile spread across his face revealing a mouth full of discolored and crooked teeth.  “Corliss how is it you found me this time” the words oozing out of his mouth like a vile sludge.  Castigan  was the worst of the worst, aside from the six murders he was wanted for, he had left a wake of  rape,  assault and theft over three territories and every time Corliss had failed in bringing him to justice , the man slipping through her fingers each time .  But not this time, this time she had caught up to  Castigan . Of the six murders he was wanted for, two of them had been fellow Wardens and one had been a close friend.  Corliss wanted  Castigan  to refuse, wanted him to resist, “It wasn’t easy  Castigan , but I am here, will you submit to my authority” she asked and for a moment felt disappointment as the man’s shoulders slumped and Corliss thought he would surrender.  She watched as his eyes shot to his left, the two men  still standing at the bar  nodding  shit  she thought,  he knew  I  would be here,  he  brought friends and  Artus’s  ass,  I  walked right into  the  trap  she chastised  herself,   the two  men   beginning  to pull their pistols.  Corliss , however,  was faster her hands a blur as  her two chrome six shooters  quickly appeared, the hammers snapping down, as  dual  bright blue  explosions  of  energy slamming into the two surprised men .  Stepping forward  Corliss  dropped the pistols, she wanted  Castigan  alive, her hands disappearing behind her back and then coming back out with  the  two midnight hatchets just in time to see  Castigan  level his own pistol at her.  With only a second to decide Corliss threw the first hatchet at the man, causing him to duck left to avoid it.  I t  slowed him  long enough for the Warden to take two steps, swiping the gun off its target with the edge of the second hatchet as blue energy exploded into a nearby table the  pistol   leaping   from  the  outlaw’s  hand with the help of the hatchets blade, both of them pausing to watch as it skittered across the floor coming to land at the feet of few patrons who quickly backed away from it, wanting no part of this  fight, both  Warden and criminal turned back to  face  each other.  Castigan  was much broader and using that to his advantage slammed his palms into Corliss’s chest, knocking her back a few feet,  he had the advantage at range,  having almost six inches of reach beyond hers . “You won’t take me alive  dirt born ,”  Castigan  taunted , Corliss’s own smile growing wider “I really hoped you would say something like  that” she  growled her free hand disappearing behind her belt  once again   as she produced  an antique straight sword.  The dark  mahogany  handle lightly held in her  pale  hand  Corliss expertly  flipped the blade, bringing it to a ready  position as she spread her feet to gain balance . Patrons began to scatter, moving out of the way to give the two room. Ironically, she noticed, they did not leave the tavern, instead opting to stay and watch the events unfolding.  Castigan  began circling her, favoring his right leg as the left dragged across the floor. Corliss nodded down to it “does it hurt  Castigan , can you feel it before it rains, does it remind you of how much of an evil shit you are” Corliss  taunted,  and the other man paused tilting his head to regard the Warden. “I think I will give you one to match Corliss, since after all you did me the honor of giving me this one” he finished nodding down to the leg.  Corliss rotated the hatchet  in her off hand , keeping the sword  in her main hand  extended towards  Castigan , every fiber of her body  wanting  to attack,  wanting  this man dead but she had a duty, a sworn oath to the crown to return him for trial and she would make good on that oath she vowed swallowing the anger that threatened to overtake her sanity at the thought of her friends broken and beaten body found not more than a week ago.  “ Castigan , you can make this easy on yourself submit and come with me for trial, otherwise face the consequences” at that last statement she gripped the weapons tighter, taking a step towards the larger man.  The sneer that spread across his face was all the warning Corliss  had  as he sprang at her, the hand he had put into the coat came out with a sword now arcing up hoping to catch the Warden by surprise, Corliss quickly dodged left , the blade missing her chin by mere millimeters .  The sword continued upward ,  Castigan  not able to change its direction quickly enough.  The Warden  easily drove the pick end of the hatchet into  Castigan’s  large biceps, while at the same time driving the tip of the sword into underside of the arm piercing the triceps.  Castigan  roared in pain   dropping  the sword ,  his hand now useless,  as he snatched back the arm , holding it close to his body.  Quickly he stepped   right  putting distance between himself and  those deadly instruments the Warden carried  as his hand shot once again into the duster producing a large black knife . “I warned you” Corliss growled waiting to see what  Castigan  would do next.  The evil bastard might have been many things but stupid wasn’t one of them he looked over the situation and then lowered the  blade , dropping it to the floor.  “You can let me go Warden. I can make it worth your while…”  Castigan  began to say as another smile spread over his face.  Corliss matched it, hers displaying more malice “There is not enough gold in all the world  Castigan ,” she said. His grin faded quickly, and with a burst of lightning-speed, he whipped a hand from behind his back as  yet  another knife, this one smaller than the other   shot forth   burying  itself  deep  into her upper arm.  Corliss hissed looking down for a moment to see what damage had been done.  Using the distraction  Castigan  launched himself at her batting the sword blade away.  Not so disabled as I thought,  she  reflected,  then he was on her slamming her to the ground his hand going into the back of his coat and producing yet another blade, this one the length of a machete as he brought it down towards Corliss’s neck.  She  quickly brought up the hatchet and winced as the loud clang of the two metal weapons slammed into each other close to her face. Pausing for a moment the hatchet slowly slid along  Castigan’s  blade the man  forcing  it  closer  towards the Warden’s throat.  It made contact with the blades guard stopping the large knife just before it pierced the soft skin of her exposed neck and with one hand Corliss held it there.  Castigan  pressing down on the weapon but he had lost a lot of blood and his exhaustion and handicap made it hard to gain the leverage he needed, but still he tried desperately to get the kill.  “Your dead Warden, your dead”  Castigan  kept repeating she could hear the strain as the man kept trying to push the weapon further towards her neck, towards her death.  She was a slight woman, but years of training and hunting had made her strong, however the weight of the large man was quickly becoming too  much  and she felt her arm begin to shake as the blade slowly advanced once again towards her neck. Stretching out her wounded arm Corliss winced in pain. Her fingers reaching, dancing over the handle of the fallen hatchet that lay so close, the large blade inching further as it bit into the delicate skin of her neck.  She bit back the panic as her fingers  refused  to get a purchase on the  weapons  handle, she felt the blood begin to pool in the shallow wound around the blade as  Castigan  pushed harder trying to drive it those last few inches  into the soft exposed skin .  Corliss felt her fingers close around the hatchet and in one fell motion spun the blade  and with  a wide arc brought the weapon around and pierced  Castigan’s  neck driving the razor-sharp end just left of the large artery, pulling it out she did it again.  Each blow piercing nerve, muscle and soft tissue. With the third blow Corliss was rewarded as her opponent let go of the knife and slumped over from loss of blood and pain.  “Damn you Corliss, may  Mephis  shrivel your tits and rot your pussy” he  slurred, his eyes going distant as he finally lost consciousness , the sour smell of beer and meat causing her to wince at the smell. Corliss rolled him off of her with a grunt of effort and sat up wincing as she moved the wounded arm , scrambling in the jacket pockets for the small first aid kid she carried there she would not let him die, this man wasn’t getting off that easy she thought .  Two hours later the Warden was climbing up on to her horse,  Castigan’s  own horse behind her as she tied the reigns to her own saddle, Corliss regarded the man, still out like a light from pain and blood loss, an old man  shambling  up poking at the fugitive as he continually shot an annoyed look to the Warden “What? Corliss asked, the old unkempt man simply grumbled and checked on  Castigan .  "The bandages will hold as long as you are gentle, you will need to change them often to prevent infection, I assume since you had me patch him up you want him alive” the  gravelly  voice intoned giving the Warden a suspicious glance.  Corliss rolled her eyes and threw the man two coins. “ Of course,  I do doc, thank you for your ministrations I will do my best to ensure they weren’t wasted” Corliss finished and then with a nod shooed the man away, with a  final  grumble he shambled into the inn.  Turning to the local  sheriff  Corliss nodded “Thank you for helping me put the bastard on the horse sheriff, he is in good hands now” she finished and with a nod he too retreated to the inn.  It was going to be a fun ride back she thought admiring her own rope skill. The large innkeeper was the last to approach coming out of the inn and walking over to Corliss. “Warden” he greeted her.  Corliss reached into a leather bag attached to her belt and threw the man down four gold sovereigns. “Master brock, I apologize for the damage to your inn and any injuries to your customers.” She finished and the Innkeeper smiled bowing slightly “May Aurtus grant you an uneventful trip” he finally said, turning and going back into his inn  himself .  Castigan  groaned behind her eliciting a smile from The Warden. Nodding at the patrons she rode out of the small town for the  two-day  ride back to the city that would deliver final justice to her prisoner.  And another fugitive brought to justice,  she thought smiling and nodding at the sour faces that stood along the few shops of the village.  Most villagers were never happy to see Warden’s unless they were the victim of a crime. Even knowing this she smiled to each villager, nodding as she passed by.    It wasn’t long until Corliss was beyond the fence and out into the territories.  Turning west she nudged the horse a little faster, hearing the grunts and moans from her prisoner as he lay lashed to his mount.  It was going to be a rough trip for poor  Castigan  she thought still smiling.  Listening, she caught the sound of hoofbeats approaching from the rear and Corliss’s smile widened as another horse pulled alongside of her.  “Apprentice  Surin , you are not only  late,  but I was forced to  truss  and place our fugitive onto the horse without you, would you like to explain to me where you were” Corliss stated forcing irritation into her tone and doing her best to hide a smile.  The exasperated teenager looked back at the town and then to his teacher and mistress, running a hand through the unruly mop of raven hair he sighed and then looked down at the ground “I’m so sorry Ghost, I was trying to get us supplies, but the shop keeper wanted to charge double because we are Wardens and said we could afford it, I told him that wasn’t fair and I wouldn’t pay double and then he said he wouldn’t sell any supplies to me, but I know we needed them so I argued with him , getting him down to one and a half of the cost, but then it took forever to load them into the packs and by the time I was done.  Well Warden you were already riding out” he blurted out and then with a wince waited for the chastising he was sure would follow his explanation. Corliss tilted her head back and laughed a deep belly laugh and then shaking her head and mumbling to herself  urged  her horse forward leaving the young apprentice confused and sitting there.  After a few moments the young man joined her “Um Ghost, what was that about?” he finally asked looking back at the town and then to Corliss.  “I am impressed  Gorkin  was able to get one and half out of you, I told him to try for three times, but I guess he felt bad for you” Corliss said conversationally.  It took the young man a few minutes before he finally put it together, at first not believing it, then as what had happened set in, he shot an irritated look at Corliss but quickly squashed it. “Mistress was this a training that I wasn’t supposed to know about, if so, did I pass,” the young man asked hopefully.  Corliss almost burst out into fresh laughter but instead repressed it. “No, young man. It’s called hazing the new guy, that’s all,  also  a piece of advice, when in the company of civilians, call me Warden Corliss, Ghost is fine in private, but never around civilian’s” she finished and for a moment  Surin  was trying to figure out how to navigate respect with the irritation he so obviously felt.  Corliss decided to let him off the hook. “ Surin , when I am not teaching you and we are just riding, if I irritate you just tell me.  One day you will be on this side of the situation and how you ask the apprentices to treat you reflects more on you than on them.  As for the hazing, relax we all go through it” she finished giving the young man a smile as they rode. “Warden  Corl ...  er Ghost, I noticed your arm is wounded, we should stop so I can treat it” the young man said, and Corliss could hear the concern in his voice.  Surin  was a good kid, a gentle kid she still didn’t know if he was going to make a good Warden, but he would be a good man and that was the best raw material to start with.  “No,  Surin , I will be fine it’s not that bad and the blood has stopped flowing so nothing critical was hit” Corliss answered him. She could tell the young man wasn’t happy about the answer, but he didn’t protest instead opting to ride in annoyed silence.  It took Corliss only a few minutes before she was tired of the quiet. “ Surin , did I ever tell you how I ended up in the  Warden’s? ” she asked her apprentice the young man leaning forward on his horse and Corliss could hear the anticipation in his voice “NO Mistress, I mean I have heard stories, but you have never talked about it” he said barely hiding the  excitement  in his tone.  Surin  had only been riding with Corliss for a few weeks, before that he had spent the better part of five years in training and then working with three previous wardens before getting paired with Corliss for his final evaluation.  Uri had told her before she left for this hunt the kid would accompany her. Uri had high hopes for the young man, and it said something as this is the first time that Corliss had been paired with an apprentice.  She just wasn’t sure if it said good things about her or the kid or both. Uri was like that he enjoyed throwing curveballs to see how you would react to them. Sitting back, she regarded the young man, so exuberant and excited about his first hunt.  Though Corliss did not know why the Lord Adjudicator for the Wardens would have him go out after  Castigan , he was incredibly dangerous which was one of the reasons she had ensured the shop keeper had kept young  Surin  busy while she was securing the fugitive.  If things had not gone her way the shopkeeper would have hid the young man until more Warden’s had arrived.  Corliss thanked the gods that wasn’t necessary. She put a smile on her face, she didn’t want to trouble the young man, but she would need to have a talk with Uri when she got back, the poor kid should have been sent on an easier assignment. Finally, turning to  Surin  who sat atop his horse waiting patiently “I was younger than you, probably about five years younger which would have made me twelve. My mother had died of fever and my father had left us years before, he had wanted a son, someone he could leave his legacy to, but instead he was given a bastard and a female one at that.  I fell in with local gangs in the capital and one day I was picking the pocket of a brutish looking fellow and he caught me” Corliss began smiling as she remembered that day well, it was the day that changed her life forever and made her what she was today.  “Instead of turning me in, the barbarian took me in and made me his apprentice, his name was Uri  Ammital , though you know him as the Lord Adjudicator” Corliss  continued,  she could see the young man lean closer to her, enraptured by the tale which she was sure had been told to him many times as a young apprentice, most did get told the tale of Corliss and her misadventures with Uri.  “Uri taught me everything I know; he was an amazing teacher and took me under his wing for many years until the day I took the vows” she finished still smiling at the thought of the man.  Though Uri had been more than a teacher, he had been like a father to Corliss when she had needed one most, following in his footsteps had been easy Corliss had worshipped the man and everything he stood for.  “Uri once told me that one person can make a difference, one person can change the course of history  should they be brave enough to stand in the way of destiny” she stated.  “Ma’am, uh…Ghost” the young man corrected, and Corliss waved a dismissive hand. “As I said  Surin , when we  ride,  I am Ghost, not  Madam  or Mistress or even Warden” she finished getting a smile of relief from the young man. “Yes Ma-, I mean Ghost” he corrected with a sheepish grin on his face.  “Is it true Lord  Ammital  taught you to be a master brawler and a master swordsman by the time you were sixteen?” he asked  hesitantly,  and Corliss chuckled. “I see old  Vegram  has been telling stories while getting you to work in the kitchen,” she said, shaking her head.  “Yes, it is true” she finally finished the young man seemed to be exploding out of his saddle “Corliss, that’s  amazing,  “he   gushed,  and Corliss waved him off.  “Mastering martial combat is not the hardest thing you will do as a Junior Warden, but it does require you to learn and master multiple ancient forms of fighting,” she finished, and  Surin  nodded, taking the advice to heart.  Every young initiate worried they would not be able to handle the fugitives and that they would fail in the eyes of their teacher Corliss knew but also knew that Uri wouldn’t send someone out unless he was absolutely sure they were ready.  They  rode  in silence for a while, Corliss thinking of why Uri would send this young man on a hunt like this, that wasn’t like him and to think of it she had never recalled an initiate being paired with a Warden on anything more than a simple courier mission or court appearance. This bothered her and Corliss didn’t know if the old man was testing her or Sorin.  Uri didn’t do anything without a reason and everything he did was a test meant to test one or both people participating that much she knew.  “Ghost,”  Surin  asked tentatively she was going to have to help the kid work on his assertiveness she thought wincing as he called for her again. “What is it  Surin ” she finally answered  “How hard is it to follow the living  oath,  I mean do you ever wish you hadn’t taken it?” he finally  asked,  and Corliss nodded this was a question every initiate eventually asked hell she had even asked it of Uri.  “I will first tell you what Lord  Ammital  told me the first time I asked him that question. The Wardens are the line between anarchy and law in the land, there is no other and if the Wardens ceased to be then the country would descend into throws of lawlessness” she started remembering when she had been given this speech.  Unlike today she thought, pulling her coat tighter ebbing the chill of the cold autumn air as she thought back to a warm summer day when a much younger Corliss had asked her master and the head of the order about the oath.  “The oath is the bond between the monarchy and the people, it is the trust that is placed into the hands of men and women to stand up against the evil in this world to ensure the victims get the justice they deserve” she repeated to  Surin  as she herself heard the words over a decade ago.  “ Surin , when we take the oath, we do agree to not get married, or have children. We agree to make justice our partner in life and that is not for everyone, but I will tell you there is no higher calling young man, but that does not mean you give up sex” she finished shooting a smile at the apprentice as his  face turned  beat red “yes Warden” he whispered but refusing to meet her eyes.  They continued to ride for a while, Corliss thinking over the young man’s  frustration, she  couldn’t blame him she too had felt the same way at his age, but Uri, well-being Uri was not always the best person to talk to “Trust your Training” was his motto and answer for everything. Shaking it off, Corliss looked over to the young man, was it her she wondered or were the apprentices getting younger and younger, dismissing the thought the Senior Warden cleared her throat to get his attention.  “ Surin , have you practiced much with your  SenPai , aside from the initial training?” She asked and watched as the young man’s face lit up.  Every apprentice relished the moment they were able to learn to use the  SenPai  she thought suppressing a smile as the young apprentice answered excitement edging his voice “Not really Warden” he said reaching up and exposing the long leather bracer that was strapped to his left arm.  Corliss looked over to see the worn bracer and smiled as the sunlight danced over the multicolored runes that had been carved from crystal and inlaid into the leather as the young man ran his fingers over them, the runes beginning to glow slightly as he summoned the power within them.  “Slow down there  Surin , let’s go over what you know before we start using it” she said and watched as his face fell a little, the young man pushing the sleeve back down to cover the magical bracer.   “So, what do you know about the  SenPai  Apprentice?” Corliss asked continuing to regard the young man. He did his best to hide the eye roll, but she still caught it and suppressed another smile. “The  SenPai  was commissioned by the first Emperor for the Warden’s, it was  crafted by the first members of the Order of the Dragon after signing the Agreement” he recited  dryly,  his answer ,  directly quoted from the textbook.  Time to throw him off a bit,  she thought.  “Okay, how is it Wardens can use  Magic? Are  we Mages?” she asked and could see another half-suppressed eye roll.  “No. Wardens are not  Mages,  nor do we wield Magic, that is the realm of the Mage and the Order, however like everyone we all descend from those with  power  so we have the ability to draw on  magic  to a minor degree, but we do not have the ability to actually use it directly, that is where the Senpai comes in , it is an imbued talisman ” he stated almost bored. SIX Father and Daughter For every child says the name of the lord when young, that name is ‘Mother’. -Book of Aurtus The arctic gust tore across the snow-covered landscape as the first flakes of the season came to the territory, bathing buildings with the dry granules of white, winter had come early this year as families burrowed into the warm safety of  there  houses, fireplaces across the land sent smoke towards the sky, from a distance it looked like pillars of black ascending to escape the earth. They paused, watching the stranger with open surprise to see anyone traveling the road in weather like this. Corliss nodded at the two boys as she passed the farm, both young men waving back and continuing to watch her long after she had passed the yard. Nodding towards Marcus the older mage stepped away from his friend, who now sat catatonic, his emotions and mind spent from the stress of the last week.  The two men stepped over to the corner of the room ensuring to keep  there  voices low as not to disturb the shopkeeper who simply sat, still staring blankly “What the hell is this about runes in the skin  Maelen , I saw your face, you know something” Marcus  asked  and the older man nodded  solemly .  “Old forbidden experiments, sounds like the Empress has found access to things best left forgotten, if she has Marcus, we are in for a world of hurt, those are mages enhanced with Runes, I have no idea how strong they are or what they are capable of , the creatures though, I have heard of them in some of the archives it tells of the failed experiments and things called Crystal Wraiths or screamers for the sound they make, they are like walking animals with a lust for blood, we need to get out of here and fast”  Maelen  said.  Marcus could see the fear in his eyes, it took everything he had to keep his calm and with a few deep breaths he steeled himself, Marcus wouldn’t leave these people, would not allow this creature to kill them for sport, he had spent the better part of the trip questioning his own morality, yes he had killed and done so in cold blood, but for the first time since  Orah’s  death he found himself set on a purpose and one he could live with. “ Maelen , I will not leave these people to  there  fate, these things are mages and it is going to take mages to deal with them, I need your help but dammit if I have to I will face them alone, I will not run from this, these people are innocent and need our help” Marcus said his words like a slap in the face for his friend.  Maelen  winced and lowered his eyes for a moment, then with a nod he met his friends eyes “Your right, but understand, I don’t know if we can survive this Marcus, if you do this, we very well could end up dead or if they take us alive, worse” he  said ,  his stare telling Marcus what he didn’t want to hear.  If they try and take you, make sure your no longer living , those eyes said. The front door of the shop opened slowly revealing the cobblestone street, moonlight played over the  builings  offering enough light to see. As Marcus stepped  out  he watched the shadows nestled between the buildings, scanning for any movement or signs of hidden enemies as the two men stepped out into the middle of the small market street. The town was a silent as a tomb the echoes of  there  footfalls shattering the stone silence as they stepped towards the town center.  Closing his eyes Marcus reached out, playing his consciousness out into the night, scanning for any sign of animal or man, as they slowly walked everything was still, like a calm before a storm.  Marcus stopped dead as his mind played over something cold and alien, the images made no  sence  as  rapid fire  graphics assaulted his senses like a macabre snuff film, holding up his hand he stopped  Maelen .  Closing his eyes he reached out, concentrating, focusing on the insane  rhythym  of the thoughts slamming into the barrier of his mind.  Finally  it became too much and he pulled back, but not before an ear splitting shriek erupted over the town, the echo’s sounding like responses.  “ Maelen , I don’t know what these things were, but they aren’t human any longer, those images” he began and shuddered when trying to describe them. Marcus focused on his friend and noticed that he wasn’t looking at him, in fact he just stood  there ,  his eyes wide , Marcus followed his gaze up the street and then saw what had his friend transfixed with fear, standing in the center of the narrow road , not more  then  a hundred feet from where they stood three figures loomed.  The one in the middle was unmistakably the Seer, he still wore the front shell of the young man’s skull, combined with the black cloak he looked like a spectral demon, but it was the creatures on either side that caught Marcus’s breath in his throat. They were almost human, but like the  shopkeep  had  descriped , they had been  twisted ,  perverted somehow.  Marcus could see energy playing over the runes on all three, the magic twisting and wrenching as if someone had forced it with  there  will to bend in ways it was never supposed to. Marcus could not understand what he was looking at and before he could ask, the three creatures began moving forward towards them.  A deep laugh boomed over the  town,  he is enhancing his voice with magic Marcus thought listening as the concert level voice seemed to come from all around them.  “Mages, you will submit to my will and that of my Empress, you will  serve  or you will die” the booming voice said as the three creatures slowly moved down the street closing the gap.  Out of the corner of his eye Marcus watched as his friend pulled the odd quarterstaff from his  back ,  except this time he didn’t extend it, instead with a twist of the center the staff came apart into two short swords, the blades engraved with runes that began to glow as  Maelen  infused it with power. “I will take the Seer, can you handle the demons?” he asked and looking at his friend, his teacher he could see the worry and doubt.  Marcus had very little training, very little experience and he was about to match his will against creatures that had been twisted with the same magic he used.  He doesn’t think I will stand a chance” he thought as a lance of fear split through his  phsyce , with a force of will he shoved it down, he had no choice, he was the only thing standing between these perversions of magic and the innocent people now cowering in  there  homes.  They might be allowing them to come out a few at a time and hunting them for sport, but they would get bored, they would eventually simply go house to house tearing people apart Marcus thought and the fear was replaced with Rage.  “Do not fret my friends, it is just us, my soldiers have gone on to scout the next village, we have some quality time before they get back, I expect by the time they return I will have new acolytes for my Empress or a few new skulls for my collection” the Seer boomed as the three continued to move towards them.  Marcus began to collect power to himself, pulling like he had never pulled before feeling the energy collect until he felt as if he would explode. “Wait for my signal”  Maelen  whispered next to him and Marcus held the magic, it was like trying to hold your breath, the longer you held  it ,  the worse it got until it felt as if he himself was on fire, but he held on, concentrating on not letting go of the power.  Maelen  stood there for two more agonizing minutes, allowing the three to get closer, with a flourish he reversed the blades, bringing them to rest against the bottom of his forearm and then with a burst of will, the old mage seemed to teleport across the distance, appearing directly in front of the Seer, for a moment the man stopped , surprised, but he had also pulled out his own staff and as  Maelen  went in for a killing blow, the two blades spun from under the robe, the silver runed blades glinting in the moonlight as they sliced and parried , the two men locked in a vicious dance of death.  Before the two demons could move in to assist Marcus thrust out his hands and with a bellow of rage released the power, the two creatures were caught off guard, both flung back almost the distance they had come, only to be brought up short by a thick stone wall on the side of the tavern. The satisfying sound of cracking stone and breaking bones echoed over the alleyway followed by screams of rage and pain.  Quickly pulling in energy Marcus thrust his palms downward and behind him, sending him flying through the air, he extended his arms sending light pushes of kinetic force against the buildings to steady himself. As he came near the  ground  he expended the rest of the energy into a soft landing thrusting his hands down and in front of him.  Marcus had no weapons, but he had power, natural power that had not been twisted and bent and he once again pulled in  energy,but  before he could replenish, one of the creatures shrieked, pushing its palms at Marcus as two fireballs shot forward, Marcus dove left and felt the heat of the fireballs singe the leather of his outfit. As he  landed  he gathered heat in his mind and pushing his will at the closest creature he watched as it ignited into a pillar of flame and smoke, its energy expended and unable to gather enough for a defense. A malicious smile spread across Marcus’s face, lit against the burning creature as it  thrashed ,  trying to put out the flames.  He was so caught up in the first creature he almost didn’t see the second one launch itself over his brethren and come barreling down towards Marcus teeth bared and claws extended. It hit him while he was still on the ground and four sets of  razor sharp  claws raked the front of the leather Mage armor, Sparks of energy flew from the leather as the armor spell held.  With a prayer of thanks to whomever had created it Marcus struggled with the creature, he grabbed both  wrists,but  the creature extended his arms, lowering himself towards the mage as his jaws snapped closed just inches from his face.  Looking into the red glowing coals the creature had for  eyes ,  this thing did look like a creature from hell he thought, straining to hold on as he desperately tried to keep the thing from  bitting  or clawing him, if the armor spell failed, of that thing managed to get those claws onto exposed skin, Marcus was  donefor  he thought, panic welling up in his mind, with an effort he forced it down, gathering power once again.  He thought desperately trying to find something he could  do  or  effect to get this thing off him, it wrapped its legs around his torso, ensuring Marcus couldn’t push it off with magic, he also couldn’t set it ablaze unless he too wished to join it. These things could reason, they could analyze a problem and come up with a solution he thought, not a mindless creature he realized and chided himself for underestimating the thing. He struggled with the thing for what seemed like an eternity, his muscles straining against the creatures own as they fought for position.  Marcus tried to get a look to see if  Maelen  might aid him, but when he looked, he could see his friend, sliced and bleeding as he was retreating from the Seer, the bone clad man advancing on his friend, it wouldn’t be long thought Marcus until  Maelen  would be dead, that thing was younger and faster and matched the old man in power.  As he lay there struggling, desperately trying to figure a way out, a way to help himself and his friend before they both wound up dead, or worse, he thought of the rabbit, the first one he had tried to  influence ,  pushing too hard had killed the creature his mind locked onto something the old man had said  Creatures changed by crystals are susceptible to manipulation, we can influence them and read  there  thoughts  . Marcus remembered the staccato of images, gathering his power, knowing he had one chance, should this  fail  he would die and so would  Maelen .  Gathering every ounce of collected energy, Marcus pictured a  razor sharp  lance and with all his will he pushed it directly into the creatures head and slamming his own will into that of the demon.  The creature tensed, its thrashing  stopped ,  then it began to convulse as Marcus pushed even more power into that lance DIE he willed pushing even harder, he felt himself beginning to  epp , beginning to weaken as darkness closed in around him, threatening to render him unconscious , but still he pushed harder, willing the last scraps of energy he had summoned into that things skull.  It stumbled off of Marcus and as he watched, it bled from its eyes and nose and mouth, it took a few staggering steps away from the young mage and collapsed, its head exploding into a mass of brain and blood.  Marcus rose to his feet unsteadily, his body on the verge of  exaughstion . Turning he found the Seer still advancing on the retreating  Maelen , he could see the things runes began to glow as it gathered power to himself.  Marcus was spent, he didn’t have the energy or the will to summon power, for a moment he stood there helpless, I need power he pleaded to his body and for a moment he was resigned to stand there watching in horror as  Maelen  was about to be  anihalated .  “ Im  an asshole” he whispered, damn near slapping his head. Taking the last of his strength he ran full speed at the Seer, the thing so focused on the kill, he didn’t even sense him coming, as he was within a few feet of the taller man, Marcus launched himself feet first bringing both of his heels against the Seers back and pushing. The Seer stumbled, surprised as he began to fall forward, the power released as his concentration was lost.  Maelen  was quick, taking advantage of the moment of distraction he thrust both of the short blades into the Seer’s torso, as Marcus watched the ends emerged from his back, pulling them out  Maelen  gathered energy and using a kinetic push, spun three hundred and sixty degrees before the Seer could recover. Its head jumped to the left of his body, falling to the ground with a meaty sound as the body stood there for a moment, as if unwilling to believe that the head was gone. Then it dropped to its knees for a long beat, before falling forward, dead.  Coming over to help his friend , the two Mages leaned on each other  Maelen  looking at the burning corpse of one and the exploded head of the other and smiled “I wouldn’t have thought of that” he said and Marcus  illicited  a tired chuckle, as they shambled back towards the Mages shop, doors began to open and people tentatively peaked  there  heads out, then they stepped slowly out of  there  houses, soon the streets were flooded with the survivors of the town.  Epilogue The fall of a nation The sun ascended above the stone shops, spreading light and warmth over the bloody streets, Marcus and  Maelen  stood, leaning on each other as they closed  there  eyes to the warmth of the coming morning.  “The soldiers will return, what do you think will happen?” Marcus asked looking back at the townsfolk, smiling as they checked on neighbors, some crying for lost friends or family.  Maelen  turned to do the same “Not sure, maybe they will leave, the death of the Seer surely will give them pause” he began “If not, these people are still in danger” he finished.  “ No  my friend, we are already distributing weapons, we will not allow the soldiers to enter this town, we no longer recognize the authority of the Black Queen”  Blavin  said approaching the two men.  He held two rifles, one of many he had handed out in the last few hours and stood smiling at the two mages “You two will always have a home here, with us” he said bowing slightly to them. Marcus lowered himself in an approximation of a bow until Vertigo forced him upright once again,  Maelen  begged  off  but Marcus took the rifle with heartfelt thank you and then proceeded to check the eight cylinder drum,  Blavin  handed him a satchel with two more drums and loose ammunition, the blue crystal spheres causing an  etherial  glow against the inside of the leather bag. “Thank you  Blavin , we were glad to help”  Maelen  answered.  Blavin’s  face fell as he reached around his back and pulled another  satchel ,  one that  Maelen  recognized, the emblem of the dragon emblazoned on the front of it. “These are all the missives that came in, as of this morning, a courier showed up in the early hours, I had a chance to review  them ,  but you are not going to like it  Maelen ” he said and handed the satchel out for the other man to take.  Maelen  took it, opening the top and pulling out a stack of parchment, standing here he began to slowly go through it as Marcus looked  on ,  watching the other man’s face as he did.  Maelen  read fast at first and then slowing down as the missives progressed, finally once he had finished, lowering his head he put them gently back in the messenger bag and handed them back to  Blavin  “Keep them safe mage” he simply said and with a nod of understanding the other man turned and walked back towards the gathered townsfolk.  Maelen  turned and began walking out towards the gate, the younger man following at  first  he was silent but then his  curiousity  got the better of him. “ Whats  wrong  Maelen , what did you see?” he whispered as they continued out of the small town. “The Empress has declared war on everyone, the Wardens are scattered the church is decimated and the Order is arguing  wether  or not to join her, Marcus, she has  broke  the agreement, if something isn’t done, war will break out” THE END
